This early summer, Apple has been hit by the global memory crisis and raised prices significantly. For example, the iPad Air went from $599 to $749, the M5 MacBook Pro from $1,699 to $1,999, and the Apple TV from $129 to $199. The above are just some examples—the point is that these increases are quite staggering.

This situation inevitably raises the question—will Apple significantly improve its products under the new pricing to make them more attractive?

Of course, some Apple products are about to undergo major revisions, with the MacBook Pro and iPad mini being two of them. But for products that won't see major updates in the short term, I really can't imagine Apple selling yesterday's specifications at much higher prices and still making consumers feel they're getting value for money—especially when compared with what's available on the second-hand market right now.

If you could buy an M4 iPad Air a few months ago for $599 (or even as low as $499), why would you pay $749 now? The higher the price, the more obvious this question becomes.

Some Apple products have gone without major changes for a long time. The iPad Air has used the same design and features since 2020, with only chip upgrades and Apple Pencil Pro support; the basic iPad has been largely unchanged since 2022; and the iMac has been more or less the same since 2021.

Do these products need a redesign? Probably not, actually. But I think Apple could do something to make them more appealing at current price points. For example, the iMac could switch to a miniLED display, the iPad Air could get a 120Hz refresh rate, or the basic iPad could get a fully laminated display.

Compared with the price increases, these upgrades would cost relatively little and should also make consumers more accepting of the new pricing. On the other hand, Apple may also lower some product specifications to offset rising costs—for example, the iPhone may once again offer a 128GB version.

What are your thoughts on Apple's product lineup after the price increases? Feel free to share in the comments section.
